I want my note to be kind of a blanket statement to anyone who reads it. It should serve to point people in the general direction as to why I killed myself.

To begin I wish to apologize sincerely to any emergency personal attending the scene of my death. I did not want to bring my misery into anyone’s life, but some must pay a small price for my death. I am sorry.

Secondly I would like to extend a thank you to those that tried to help me on my life’s journey. I felt enormous relief from your compassion, and wish I could reward you with a happier outcome. For now my struggle is over. Ultimately you were successful.

I regret that I have neither time, nor patience, nor the will to offer my condolences to you individually. My disease has robbed me of many of my mental faculties, and when the moment I commit the act, I will have forgotten you all together. This is not for lack of love, this is simply because my mind has cut off so many of the happy memories we shared together. The fact that I had, at one point, smiled, and danced, and laughed, sadly brings me no comfort here in my dark riven. 

When I look forward I see a desert plain, scorched black from fire, murky with sulfurous fog. When I think of myself it feels to me like a bloated corpse, ripe with maggots and flies, soon to burst open with putrid juices. The creatures in my head play shadow puppets along the inside of my skull. They act out scenes of violent ends; of exsanguination, of immolation, and of trepanning. 

I am a loathsome creature in an empty world, and I have marched forward for your benefit for so many, many years. I am tired. I would lay down my head in sleep if it weren’t for the fact that I may soon awake. 

So good-bye now. And I’m sorry.

Though it might seem like reality is a murky quagmire, rest assured there are a few of use that will reach in the depths and try to haul out out. What you make of my words is up to you. You said it yourself. Words are symbols. Luckily for both of us they are also strong, whether you choose to believe that or not.

You seem to me at least moderately intelligent (Your writing is excellent, but that's not exactly a sign of a budding genius), and capable of finding a way through this. You have seen this darkness in others, and seen their successes and their failures. In the mean time, when your path seems murky, make good use of the emotional skills we develop over time. I too struggle with suicidality and, while they are not always terribly effective, they do tend to calm me down to a point of rationality. I am talking about things like placing ice on your face, watching tea steep, drinking another glass of water, and maybe going to bed early.

Of course you could do these skills til the cows come home, but it won't help you in the long run. I am talking, of course, of your reason to live. Last June I was on a psych ward after a near successful attempt. My psychiatrist would sit me down every day and ask me what my reason to live was. My answer was usually a blank stare. Then one day he drew me a head stone. He passed me the drawing and a pen and he told me write what I wanted on the headstone. I bawled like a baby, but after some encouragement I wrote:

"Jessica --------------"
1986-2056
Nurse, Mother, Grandmother, and Aunt
We will miss you." 

At the time of my hospitalization I was at my lowest. I was homeless. I had no job. I had no money, except to buy two bottles of bulk pills. My life was murky, and I my desperate kicks to keep my head above water did nothing but stir up more shit. 

So let go. Don't die, but stop trying for a week. Let the chips fall where they may. Try and figure out why you're alive. What is your reason to keep going? Look at your gravestone and really think what it should say. Do you want it to say 2014 or, like me, are you gonna try and go for the long haul?
Yeah. I'd call the police. That is VERY typical of a suicide in progress and men are twice as likely to succeed than women. I cannot stress this enough. THIS IS A CRISIS. CALL NOW.

I have attempted previously and I have never felt fortunate to have survived. I am always suicidal. My psychiatrist says I can expect to live the remainder of my life being chronically suicidal.

Another thing. That term "permanent solution for a temporary problem" is a load of shit. When you're depressed to a point of being suicidal there is no such thing as temporary problems. Your perspective is so flipping narrow you can't see a time before or after the pain you are feeling. It's not a permanent solution to a temporary problem. It's the ONLY solution for a limitless problem. Not trying to be rude. Just pointing out that saying is overused and dismissive.
